questions: Are your hand movements happening without your intending to move them?
Can you stop the movements when you try?
Does one hand ever move as if it has a mind of its own?
Are you fully aware during the movements?
Do you lose awareness or become unresponsive during an episode?
Do the movements occur while you are asleep?
Did they begin after a stroke, head injury, surgery, or other neurological illness?
Do you have weakness in either arm or leg?
Do you have numbness or loss of sensation on one side?
Have you had trouble speaking, understanding speech, seeing, or walking?
Do you experience an urge or inner restlessness before the movements?
Can the movements be reduced by concentrating on another task?
Do the movements worsen when someone watches you?
Have you recently started, stopped, or changed any medications?
Have you ever had similar episodes before?
results: 1. medication, supplement and herbal history: long-term hepatotoxic traditional Chinese medicine, notably Psoralea corylifolia, plus manganese-containing supplements
2. liver function and albumin/globulin: albumin 35.1 g/L (ref 35-52), globulin 30.8 g/L RAISED (ref 15-30), A/G ratio 1.14 LOW (ref 1.2-2.4)
3. whole-blood manganese: ELEVATED; fell after the supplements were stopped but remained above normal
4. brain MRI: bilateral T1 HYPERINTENSITY in the basal ganglia - manganese deposition
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Acquired hepatocerebral degeneration due to manganese neurotoxicity from cirrhosis caused by long-term hepatotoxic Psoralea corylifolia use, compounded by manganese-containing supplements

ALTERNATIVE: Manganese-induced parkinsonism

ALTERNATIVE: Hepatic encephalopathy with extrapyramidal movements

ALTERNATIVE: Wilson disease with basal-ganglia movement disorder
dx: Acquired hepatocerebral degeneration due to manganese neurotoxicity from cirrhosis caused by long-term hepatotoxic Psoralea corylifolia use, compounded by manganese-containing supplements
